RETESTING THE EXTREME ZONE & THE LOGIC BEHIND BANK MOVEMENTS

The market didn’t revisit the extreme zone by accident—it returned to close a banking order that was positioned around the 50% mark of a wick. On the lower timeframes, we can spot liquidity within the wick, but on the higher timeframes, like the Daily, the story becomes clearer: the market shifted direction and formed a new Higher High (HH).

Here's the key: the market always pulls back to the last order that pushed it forward—the one that caused the recent HH or LL—before continuing the move. That’s why we must analyze higher timeframes first and then fine-tune entries on lower ones. Only when we combine both can we see the true narrative unfold.

Smaller timeframes always follow the structure of the higher ones. Banks move capital, revisit their positions to reinvest, and then drive the market where they want it to go. Our job is not to predict—it’s to respond to their inevitable reactions, once we truly understand how the market breathes.
